I was in the navy so I don't know how particularly applicable this will be but I can make some educated guesses about the seafaring specifics.

You'll be on a watch rotation underway. In port fewer watches are manned because fewer watches are needed (you aren't worried about running into things in port, running equipment, or pirates). That aside these ships have a good bit of work to do in port. They need to load on supplies, take on water, electricity, and do maintenance you can't do underway (this can destroy a port visit). I don't know how commercial ships do it but in the navy we had duty days in port (you work every so many days in port). I imagine it would be something similar depending largely on the turn around time. Port calls are fun but it's not entirely like being on vacation. You get dropped off in some shitty part of town (if you live in a port city this will make more sense to you) and spend entirely too much money getting drunk and eating food (even if you don't drink now you will then).
As far as being sick, it depends on how sick you are. There's a strong pressure to man the watch bill (at least in the navy). If you're sick you better be really sick. If you are they confine you to your rack until you're better. The watchbill gets shifted around and everything gets taken care of. Everyone has other duties than standing watch. Depending on the watch station/ship this may or may not be allowed.
